 Judgment

Though matter is listed for hearing on admission, with consent of learned counsel for both parties,
matter is taken up for final disposal.

2. Challenging impugned judgment and award dated 22.07.2017 passed by X Additional District and Sessions Judge & MACT, Belagavi, in MVC No.2641/2014, this appeal is filed by claimants seeking for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: X Additional District and Sessions Judge & MACT, Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Brief facts as stated are that in an accident that occurred on 09.10.2014, one Sri. Ganapti Iragar who was driving truck bearing registration no.KA.22/A-7818 dashed his truck against hind portion of another truck bearing Reg.no.KA.01/AC-3259 which was stationed on highway.

As a result,
Prabhakar S/o Virupaxi Ankali who was traveling in truck bearing registration no.KA.22/A-7818 died on spot.
4. Alleging loss of dependency, his parents, wife and minor children had filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against owners and insurers of both trucks.
5. On contest by insurers on all counts, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.
Claimant no.1 and another were examined as PW1 and PW2.
Exs. P1 to P10 were marked.
In rebuttal, copy of insurance policy was got marked as Ex.R1 on consent.

6. On consideration, tribunal held that accident occurred due to negligence of driver of both lorries apportioned in ratio of 25% in case of truck bearing Reg.no.KA.01/AC-3259 and 75% in case of truck bearing registration no.KA.22/A- 7818.
It assessed compensation of Rs.16,25,000/- with interest p.a.
Not satisfied with quantum of compensation, claimants are in appeal.
7. Sri. Ashok A.Naik learned counsel for claimants - appellants submitted that tribunal failed to add future prospects and award under conventional heads was inadequate.

Learned counsel for appellants also sought for award of interest at more than 6% p.a.
8.
On other hand, Smt. Preeti Shashank, learned counsel for respondent-insurer supported award and opposed enhancement.

9. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award and record.
10.
From above submission finding of tribunal regarding negligence has attained finality.

As only claimants are seeking enhancement, only point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
11.

Insofar as income, though claimants stated that deceased was earning Rs.12,000/- p.m.+
Rs.6,000/- bhata, they did not lead any specific evidence to substantiate same.

In absence of specific Smt. Mahadevi W/O Prabhakar Ankali vs Sri. Shivashankar S/O Palaniappan on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24448150/
4 evidence, it has to be assessed notionally.

entities.text: Prabhakar Ankali vs Sri. Shivashankar S/O Palaniappan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering Exs.P8 to P10, driving licence and driving licence extract, tribunal assessed his monthly income as Rs.10,000/- though notional income for said period is Rs.7,500/-.
In view of above circumstance, assessment of monthly income would be appropriate.
12. Admittedly, claimants are wife, two minor children and parents, i.e. five dependents.
Deceased was 34 years old driver i.e. self employed

. Hence, as per decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 6 claimants would be entitled for addition of '40%' towards future prospects, deduction towards personal expenses would have to be at '1/4 t h ' and multiplier applicable would be '16'.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, loss of dependency would be Rs.20,16,000/-.
Apart from above, they would be entitled to award of Rs.40,000/- each towards spousal consortium, filial consortium and parental consortium, i.e. total of Rs.2,00,000/-.
In addition, they would be entitled for Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.

Since more than three years have lapsed after decision in Pranay Sethi (supra), there has to be addition of 10% to award under conventional heads, i.e. Rs.23,000/-.
13.

Thus, total re-assessed compensation is as follows:-
Sl.no. Heads Amount 1. Loss of dependency 20,16,000/-
 (10,000+40%-1/4X12X16)

2. Funeral expenses 15,000/-
3. Loss of estate 15,000/-
4. Loss of consortium (40000X5) 2,00,000/-
5.
Therefore, point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative.

15. In result, I pass following:
ORDER a. Appeal is allowed in part.
b.
Claimants are entitled for reassessed compensation of Rs.22,69,000/- as against Rs.16,25,000/- awarded by tribunal with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till realisation.
c. Insurers are directed to deposit enhanced compensation within six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
